note: Researched registry of lead SUPPLY sources for the GS Allude marketplace. Every entry states what is VERIFIED (page read on the date shown) vs UNVERIFIED. THE HARD RULE, evidenced across the industry: BUYING A LEAD IS NOT PERMISSION TO RESELL OR REDISTRIBUTE IT. A downstream marketplace needs an explicit supplier agreement (insertion order or publisher/vendor contract) that names the downstream recipients, channels and per-lead buyer caps. Until such a signed agreement exists for a given row, resale_status stays 'NOT AUTHORIZED' and the row must not receive consumer data.

sources.name: Contactability (SmartFinancial network) — publisher program
sources.what: Publisher program in the health insurance vertical: pay per lead / call / click, embedded JS forms, Ping Post and Host-and-Post APIs, account dashboard, monthly payments.
sources.integration: JS embed + Ping Post / Host-and-Post API
sources.targeting: Health vertical named publicly; rates not public
sources.consent: Buyer-side relationship; consent handling follows their form/network setup (TrustedForm-style capture expected)
sources.exclusivity: Shared vs exclusive not published; defined by insertion order
sources.resale_status: NOT AUTHORIZED by default. Their advertiser terms (contactability.com/pages/terms.html) say the buyer may not resell or transfer a lead's consumer information to third parties unless the insertion order expressly permits it. Our use here is the SELLER/publisher side, not buyer-side resale.
sources.fit: STRONGEST candidate for supply INTO our marketplace: we would be the publisher (we own traffic via organic/channel work and monetize it), while the marketplace only distributes leads we generate ourselves.
sources.next_step: OWNER DECISION: apply as a publisher when the site is live. Requires: domain, real consent stack, permission to send our consumer leads through their network instead.

sources.name: IntegrityCONNECT leads marketplace
sources.what: Multi-vendor lead purchasing marketplace with vendor options, real-time and custom campaigns; publishes lead-generator guidelines for its vendors.
sources.integration: Vendor onboarding + dashboard (vendor API specs in their guidelines)
sources.consent: Strongest published seller-side rules: disclose domains/publishers/methods, document express written consent, retain retrievable proof (TrustedForm/Jornaya), identify first-party vs affiliate sourcing; shared-aged leads capped at 3 advertisers with per-advertiser consent
sources.exclusivity: Sellers must label leads shared or exclusive; caps published for certain shared aged leads
sources.resale_status: NOT AUTHORIZED by default. Guidelines govern SELLERS (us as lead vendor). They document seller responsibilities, not a buyer's right to relicense.
sources.fit: Applying as a VENDOR (selling our own generated leads into their marketplace) is a legitimate supply-side path once real leads exist and consent can be evidenced to their standard.
sources.next_step: Only when real consented leads flow: review vendor agreement, confirm TrustedForm/Jornaya capture meets their rules, then apply.

sources.name: InsureLeads — ACA/health leads with developer hub
sources.what: Vendor selling ACA/under-65 leads; developer page describes real-time webhook POSTs, REST API, dashboard-configured endpoint, TLS, webhook signatures, CRM integrations.
sources.consent: Payloads can include consent fields/tokens (Jornaya LeadiD, TrustedForm) per their developer page
sources.exclusivity: Exclusive campaigns described; exclusivity and return terms belong in the order
sources.access: Per-lead pricing; confirm rate card and minimums directly

verified.level: VENDOR CLAIMS (docs read; delivery not validated)

sources.resale_status: NOT AUTHORIZED by default. No public downstream redistribution grant. Each delivery recipient must be covered by the agreement.
sources.fit: Their webhook/API model matches our delivery layer. IF a supply agreement covers our buyers as named recipients, inventory could flow through our routing. Otherwise it is a buy-side only source.
sources.next_step: Get written answers: (1) sample leads + consent artifacts, (2) may leads be forwarded to our named marketplace buyers, (3) per-lead pricing/minimums.

sources.name: QuoteWizard (buy-side lead platform, LendingTree)
sources.what: Established buyer-facing platform: consumer quote forms across owned and partner sites, real-time filtering, email/CRM delivery.
sources.integration: Email / CRM delivery; no general seller API verified
sources.targeting: Health products incl. major medical and short-term; territory and volume caps
sources.exclusivity: Sells each lead to at most four agents (claims; health-page figures displayed inconsistently — confirm actual health cap)
sources.resale_status: NOT AUTHORIZED by default. No resale grant on any reviewed page. As a small marketplace we cannot buy leads here and resell them; there is no obvious publisher-entry path verified.
sources.fit: Reference for market pricing/sharing norms (<=4 buyers/lead). Potential PARTNER-consortium idea: negotiate a shared-supply arrangement only with legal approval.

sources.name: NextGen Leads — health leads
sources.what: Buy-side platform for under-65 shoppers from owned-and-operated sites; dashboard targeting; second-price auction.
sources.integration: Dashboard delivery; no publisher program reviewed
sources.exclusivity: Page claims health data leads are exclusive; calls charged by billable duration (confirm in contract)
sources.access: Published ballpark: $4 data leads; $35 call leads
sources.resale_status: NOT AUTHORIZED by default. No resale grant found.
sources.fit: Useful benchmark pricing ONLY. Also: contributes evidence that 'data leads' (form fills) price around single-digit dollars vs $30+ call connects — context for our per-lead pricing.

sources.name: MediaAlpha — publisher monetization exchange
sources.what: Ad exchange where insurance publishers monetize click/lead/call traffic via real-time advertiser bidding.
sources.integration: Publisher onboarding via demo; API/ad units unspecified publicly
sources.targeting: Broad insurance verticals; ACA health inventory participation NOT confirmed (agent page lists auto/home/life)
sources.resale_status: NOT AUTHORIZED by default. Note the FTC context: in Aug 2025 Assurance IQ and MediaAlpha paid a combined $145M settlement over alleged misleading marketing of health insurance, incl. telemarketing/robocall practices (ftc.gov). Due diligence beyond a contract is warranted.
sources.fit: Possible click-style monetization for our organic pages LATER. Compliance history is a caution flag, not a barrier, but means we should model our own practices on cleaner standards.
sources.next_step: Optional: demo call after first real traffic; do not funnel consented phone consumer data into click exchanges.

sources.name: Smart and Simple / SASid — branded enrollment affiliate
sources.what: Branded enrollment/referral portal with call center and licensed staff; affiliates earn per enrollment; products incl. major medical, short-term, dental/vision, accident, life.
sources.integration: Branded portal (lead capture happens on THEIR branded stack)
sources.targeting: Groups, associations, SMBs, niche marketing teams named
sources.consent: Captured by SASid's own enrollment flow
sources.resale_status: NOT AUTHORIZED by default. This is a revenue-share referral arrangement, not a lead-feed sale: compensation flows per enrollment.
sources.fit: Complementary rather than supply: could monetize enrollments our channel produces without buying broker coordination infra. Compare economics against our agent-buyer pricing.
sources.next_step: Low priority; revisit if organic enrollments appear.

sources.name: Pivot Health partners

sources.resale_status: NOT AUTHORIZED by default (data rights not public).

sources.next_step: Evaluate as fallback routing destination when our own buyer roster is thin.

sources.name: ActiveProspect TrustedForm (consent certificate infra)
sources.what: Certificate documenting the consumer's form-session consent event; certificate URL flows WITH the lead to the buyer.

sources.fit: Roadmap item for buyer trust at volume: integrate Certify on the Check consent page and pass certificate URLs in deliveries the way InsureLeads-type payloads do. Budget owner approval needed (per-lead verify costs).
sources.next_step: OWNER DECISION: adopt once real volume and a real buyer exist (docs/FIRST_BUYER_PILOT.md upgrade).

sources.name: GS Allude FIRST-PARTY (our own pages, our own consent stack)
sources.what: The Health Coverage Check: consumer submits their own phone with recorded consent (one-to-one naming the platform). This is the ONLY supply path where consent, exclusivity and provenance are fully under our control.

sources.consent: Versioned consent template re-rendered server-side; timestamp, IP, UA, page URL, form snapshot SHA-256 stored
sources.exclusivity: Exclusive by design (sale_type='EXCLUSIVE', one successful delivery per lead, enforced in SQL)
sources.access: FREE except channel costs we already test at $0

verified.level: BUILT AND TESTED in this repo (270 tests)

sources.resale_status: Full authority — we are the named consent party ('{brand} and its licensed agent partner') and the operator records every sale.
sources.fit: The strategy conclusion: no external source can start the marketplace because NO external source grants provenance, exclusivity and 2026-grade consent evidence without agreements we do not have. Every external row above is a LATER supply diversification step, gated on signatures.
